main_text.p: Posteriora illa sana non sunt: ἰδία πάλιν, ὅ, σὺ π[?]ὸ [illegible, ~20 letters]. Quid enim praecipit [illegible, ~12 letters] cum sequatur, [illegible, ~15 letters]. Rescribo, [illegible, ~10 letters] nominatim ἰδία, [illegible, ~8 letters] singulos compellari dicit, [illegible, ~10 letters] exempli gratia, Δημοσθένης Δημοσθένους, nam ita compellare solebant, ὁ Demosthenes Demosthenis fili. Sed ad Tertulliani verba redeamus, qui nihil hac in parte de silentio: neque enim erant [illegible, ~12 letters], vt constat è Libanio, sed tantum de morae caussa, dicit enim annum interpositum fuisse inter [illegible, ~10 letters] Mysteriis, [illegible, ~10 letters], vt opinionem maiestatis his Mysteriis conciliaret suspendio cognitionis, & cupiditatem differendo atque procrastinando praestruerent. Postrema horum Mysteriorum scena [?]ἐποπτεία reftat, quae his verbis explicatur: Sequitur iam silentij officium, attente custoditur, quod tarde inueniter. Ceterum tota in adytis diuinitas, tot suspiria Epoptarum, totum signaculum linguae, simulacrum membri virilis reuelatur. Quibus verbis significat, grande illud arcanum, quod in adytis seruabatur, quodque tantopere sibi Epoptis reuelari exoptabant, & precibus multisque suspiriis contendebant Mystae, neque prodere licebat, simulacrum membri virilis fuisse. Non solebant autem olim eos, qui ciues Athenienses non essent, his initiare Mysteriis:

Meminit huius Legis Scholiastes Aristophanis ad Plutum: [illegible, ~12 letters] Ἀλκιβιάδης, μυσίνα ξένον μύειν. Apollodorus Lib.II.agens de Hercule: [illegible, ~12 letters]. Optime autem dixit ἐπὶ, non enim aetate sua id obseruabant: sed primitus nemo initiabatur, qui ciuis Athenienfis non esset: quare Hercules, itemque Castor & Pollux in ciuitatem adsciti sunt adoptati, hi quidem ab Aphidno, ille vero à Pylio. Plutarchus in Thefeo: [illegible, ~20 letters] Castor & Pollux, [illegible, ~25 letters] Hercules [illegible, ~10 letters], atq; ciues Δημοτικοὶ Eleusiniis Mysteriis initiati sunt: estque ex his emaculandus Apollodori codex loco laudato: [illegible, ~30 letters], Ευμολπος, [illegible, ~10 letters] Ελλοῦσα, [illegible, ~20 letters]. Ἐπεὶ δὲ Ἄμπος Πυλίῳ πᾶς ἀφιέμενος ἐμυεῖτο. Thespius Herculis coxeus is non est, qui à Pylio adoptatus est, itaque reponendum est: Ἴσ μὲν Πυλίῳ πᾶς ἀφιέμενος ἐμυεῖτο. Legitimus factus adoptione Pylij filius, ac proinde ciuis Athenienfis, initiatus est. Postea omnibus Graecis id concessum est, vt his Mysteriis possent initiari. Herodotus Lib. VIII. [illegible, ~30 letters] Μηδείας [illegible, ~10 letters] Κόρῃ, [illegible, ~15 letters] ἄλλων Ἑλλήνων, μυείσθαι. Neque tantū Graeci initiati sunt, sed quaecumque etiam aliae gentes. Cicero de Nat.Deorum Lib.I. Omitto Eleusinam sanctam illam, & angustam,

Cùm hac tamen, puto, cautione, si Graecè scirent: colligo ex his Libanij verbis iam ante laudatis, Declamatione XIX. [illegible, ~20 letters] Ἐπὶ δὲ τὸ Ἀπάτης [illegible, ~10 letters] Ἑλλήνων, μυείσθαι. Neque tantū Graeci initiati sunt, sed quaecumque etiam aliae gentes. Sub-

page.notes: The Greek lines at the top of the page and in the body are small and blurred. Most Greek words could not be read letter by letter, so they are marked as illegible or with [?]. The Greek in the body (for example the Herodotus and Libanius passages) is a best approximation and should be checked against a sharper scan. The top shaded band is a scan artefact and is not printed text. The bottom-right "Google" watermark is a digitiser's mark and was left out. The line ending "Sub-" runs on to the catchword "mouebantur".
